title: Consume European signed task lookup projection
changes: Publish the authenticated four-byte signed projection at 371020..371024 in E206-d205 while leaving the original unsigned guest index uncapped and composing with adjacent owners.
Preserve previous task parameter fields and usage counters; separately track the represented lookup bytes and indices.
validation: Windows test build e214-signed-build-ybvdt2ef and EUR Wine e214-signed-wine-qo5za07r pass every represented byte, mixed boundaries and mirrors, 122 preserved resources, authenticated source, owner retention, and 24 interpreter/generated-dispatch reader cases across 12 indices including 255.

EUR Wine e214-home-scene-wine-aj4omulx matches full state, guest clock, video, OAM, dispatch and five nonempty audio streams across 600 recorded home frames with the projected ROM backing altered; indices 1 and 2 are served.

Windows production build e214-cli-build-3fbjudfd and EUR Wine e214-signed-cli-wine-yozdoyrs pass create/reuse/verify with 124 files matching the tested dataset. Static e214-home-residual-jd33pjgk leaves 2108 of the original 8544 sampled bytes unowned, all below 300000.
limitations: Only four physical bytes are projected, not a complete inferred guest table. Other indices, consumers, executing PCs in the scene, scenes, real-BIOS and UI save/Load remain open. Linux, USA and native Windows require separate verification. No performance comparison was performed.
Earlier linear reader-window evidence 7zra4rc1 contains a D-Bus assertion. New Wine tests use the local overlay, show no such assertion and drain their servers.
